question: Should ClawHub/OpenClaw continue supporting the legacy `molt.bot` curl-piped installer path, or should it be retired/redirected to the current documented install flows?
rationale: The failing installer source is not tracked in current ClawHub main, and the live hosted script has changed, so automation cannot safely choose whether to patch a legacy external path or move users away from it.

options.title: Retire or redirect legacy installer
options.body: Point `molt.bot` users to the current OpenClaw/ClawHub install commands and document the supported Node range instead of maintaining an untracked legacy zsh path.

options.title: Support and track the installer
options.body: Bring the hosted installer source under a maintained repository path, then reproduce and harden the unmatched npm cleanup glob on macOS/Homebrew zsh.

options.title: Wait for fresh reporter data
options.body: Keep the issue waiting on a current reproduction if maintainers are not ready to decide the legacy installer boundary.

recommendation.title: Retire or redirect legacy installer
recommendation.body: Point `molt.bot` users to the current OpenClaw/ClawHub install commands and document the supported Node range instead of maintaining an untracked legacy zsh path.

likelyOwner.reason: The current maintained CLI/install surfaces and docs in this checkout are attributed to Patrick-Erichsen in blame and PR metadata.
